frozenset-readmostly.title: Use FrozenSet for read-mostly sets
frozenset-readmostly.short: Freeze a set that will be searched repeatedly
frozenset-readmostly.summary: FrozenSet<T> represents a set that is not modified after construction and is optimized for repeated lookup.
frozenset-readmostly.why: It suits data such as configuration values or reserved words that is built once and queried many times with Contains.
frozenset-readmostly.tips: Construction has a cost, so compare it with HashSet<T> when the set is rebuilt frequently.

priorityqueue-minheap.title: Dequeue items by priority with PriorityQueue
priorityqueue-minheap.short: Process the item with the smallest priority first
priorityqueue-minheap.summary: PriorityQueue<TElement,TPriority> stores elements with priorities and dequeues the element with the smallest priority.
priorityqueue-minheap.why: It directly supports algorithms such as Dijkstra and work scheduling where the next highest-priority item must be selected repeatedly.
priorityqueue-minheap.tips: Ordering among equal priorities is not stable. Include a sequence value in the priority when deterministic tie ordering matters.

task-completionsource-async-continuation.title: Run TaskCompletionSource continuations asynchronously
task-completionsource-async-continuation.short: Avoid running await continuations inline with completion
task-completionsource-async-continuation.summary: TaskCreationOptions.RunContinuationsAsynchronously prevents TaskCompletionSource completion from directly running waiting continuations inline.
task-completionsource-async-continuation.why: Low-level adapters from callbacks to Task can avoid surprising reentrancy or heavy continuation work on the thread that signals completion.
task-completionsource-async-continuation.tips: Use TaskCompletionSource to bridge external completion events into Tasks; do not use it as a replacement for ordinary async methods.

parallel-foreachasync-bounded.title: Bound concurrency with Parallel.ForEachAsync
parallel-foreachasync-bounded.short: Run asynchronous item work with a fixed concurrency limit
parallel-foreachasync-bounded.summary: Parallel.ForEachAsync processes elements concurrently and lets you cap concurrency with MaxDegreeOfParallelism.
parallel-foreachasync-bounded.why: It can improve throughput without sending an unbounded number of operations to an external service or shared resource.
parallel-foreachasync-bounded.tips: More concurrency is not always faster. Measure with the limits of the target service and the CPU or I/O characteristics of the work.

searchvalues-span.title: Reuse SearchValues for repeated Span searches
searchvalues-span.short: Search for any of the same candidates efficiently
searchvalues-span.summary: SearchValues<T> prepares a candidate set that APIs such as Span.IndexOfAny can reuse across searches.
searchvalues-span.why: It expresses repeated scans for the same separators or characters without rebuilding the candidate representation for every input.
searchvalues-span.tips: For a single short search, a direct IndexOfAny call may be simpler. Measure on representative input before optimizing.

xmlreader-streaming.title: Stream large XML documents with XmlReader
xmlreader-streaming.short: Read forward without materializing the whole document
xmlreader-streaming.summary: XmlReader reads XML as a forward-only stream and also supports asynchronous reading.
xmlreader-streaming.why: Large XML documents can be processed when relevant elements arrive instead of building a complete DOM in memory.
xmlreader-streaming.tips: Enable XmlReaderSettings.Async for async APIs and review safe parser settings when input is not trusted.

incrementalhash-stream.title: Hash large data incrementally with IncrementalHash
incrementalhash-stream.short: Compute a digest without buffering all input
incrementalhash-stream.summary: IncrementalHash accepts successive chunks through AppendData and produces the digest when the stream is complete.
incrementalhash-stream.why: Large files or network payloads can flow directly into hashing without first becoming one large byte array.
incrementalhash-stream.tips: Choose a hash appropriate to the purpose; do not use a general fast hash directly for password storage.

aesgcm-authenticated-encryption.title: Encrypt with authentication using AesGcm
aesgcm-authenticated-encryption.short: Produce ciphertext and an authentication tag together
aesgcm-authenticated-encryption.summary: AesGcm provides AES-GCM authenticated encryption, producing ciphertext plus a tag that detects modification.
aesgcm-authenticated-encryption.why: It provides confidentiality and integrity together instead of requiring a custom combination of encryption and a MAC.
aesgcm-authenticated-encryption.tips: Never reuse a nonce with the same key. Define key, nonce, and tag sizes and their storage format as part of the protocol.

random-shared.title: Use Random.Shared for general-purpose randomness
random-shared.short: Avoid managing a shared Random instance yourself
random-shared.summary: Random.Shared exposes a thread-safe shared Random instance for ordinary non-cryptographic random values.
random-shared.why: General application code can avoid repeatedly constructing Random instances or synchronizing a shared instance manually.
random-shared.tips: Use RandomNumberGenerator for keys, tokens, and other values that require unpredictability.

conditionalweaktable-metadata.title: Attach metadata with ConditionalWeakTable
conditionalweaktable-metadata.short: Associate data without extending the key object's lifetime
conditionalweaktable-metadata.summary: ConditionalWeakTable<TKey,TValue> associates values with reference-type keys without preventing those keys from being collected.
conditionalweaktable-metadata.why: It can attach metadata to objects you cannot modify while avoiding the strong-key retention of a normal Dictionary.
conditionalweaktable-metadata.tips: It is not a general dictionary replacement. Use it specifically for auxiliary data whose lifetime should follow its key.
